title: Show any object's fields on the support page

blocks.text: The support team's diagnostics page shows the state of an order, a session or a cart: every field next to its value. `FieldReader.read(object)` builds that table and already works out the names; it needs two helpers in `src/main/java/practice/FieldReader.java`:

items: `instanceFields(type)`: the fields an object of that type carries. Support wants the whole state, not only the parts a class chose to expose, and static fields are not state;
`value(field, object)`: the field's value in that object.

blocks.text: Support also opens objects whose class comes from the JDK, such as the plain `ArrayList` behind a cart. For those the page must still render, with `FieldReader.HIDDEN` in place of each value the JVM won't let the reader see. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: the instance fields of a plain object are shown with their values, and static fields are left out
private fields are listed, not only public ones
a private field of the application's own class is opened and its value shown, not hidden
fields declared by a superclass, private ones included, are part of the object's state
an object whose class is inside the JDK is shown with every value hidden instead of failing

origin.section: setAccessible Opens Private Members of Class-Path Code, Not of the JDK

concepts: getDeclaredFields() lists one class's own fields, private ones included; a superclass's private fields are listed by its own Class, and getFields() returns only public ones.

setAccessible(true) opens private members of class-path code but throws the unchecked InaccessibleObjectException on JDK internals unless the package is opened; trySetAccessible() answers false instead.
